title: Does a low audit rate for coder-negatives pay when the coder has high recall?
summary: On 3,188 real GoEmotions comments, three automated coders (naive-Bayes cut-offs coding 2, 3 and 4 times the human positive share; recall 0.72, 0.90, 1.00; not LLMs) and a hand-coded audit of 100 to 400 items. The best share of the audit among coder-negatives falls as recall rises (about 50%, 20%, 2% or lower), following the oracle Neyman share (0.43, 0.18, 0). But the narrowest 95% interval at 200 items (0.115 to 0.119) is no better than a plain random audit of 200 items with no coder (0.1195), because precision is only 0.25–0.36. Coverage still fails at low shares unless the negative stratum is almost clean (worst coder 0.48 at 2%, 0.77 at 5%, 0.91 at 10%). Bias is removed in every cell by weighting. Recall is bought with low precision by moving a weak classifier's cut-off; an LLM with both high is untested. One code, one corpus, one split; Wald intervals; no finite-population correction.
lede: does a low audit rate for coder-negatives pay when the coder has high recall? On 3,188 GoEmotions comments the best share falls with recall (50%, 20%, 2%), but the narrowest interval (0.115–0.119 at 200 items) only matches a random audit with no coder (0.1195). Not an LLM.
